items.title: In differentially closed fields the non-minimality degree agrees with the fibre dimension
items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that in the theory of differentially closed fields the non-minimality degree of a type agrees with its fibre dimension F_ind (statement lines 442-444). The proof first reduces to types without proper fibrations through the behaviour of F_ind along an analysis, then invokes the classification of such types into a locally modular case and a case internal to a non-locally-modular type (proof line 446-451). The step that carries the content is the second case: the proof has to move from generic 2-transitivity of the binding group to a definable isomorphism with a multiply transitive algebraic group action, where Knop's classification leaves only the affine and the projective actions, and then exhibit a Morley sequence on a line to obtain the value 2 for both invariants (proof lines 451-455). The first case is immediate, and the reduction is a citation plus one estimate. H2.
